  Catalogue of works by the artists John Baldessari shown in an art exhibition at the Sprengel Museum Hannover 26.9.1999 - 2.1.2000. The purpose of the prototype is to demonstrate how to catalogue artworks in an exhibition as Linked Open Data on Wikidata. In this instance an OCR scan is transfered to Wikidata and then ouput as a computationally reproducible Quarto publication.

# About the original exhibition

Exhibition title: 'while something is happening here, something else is happening there ; works 1988 - 1999' ; Spectrum - Internationaler Preis für Fotografie der Stiftung Niedersachsen 

Location: 

Sprengel-Museum Hannover, 26.9.1999 - 2.1.2000.

Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Gemäldegalerie Neue Meister, 15.1. - 2.4.2000. 

Sprengel Museum website: [https://www.sprengel-museum.de/ausstellungen/archiv](https://www.sprengel-museum.de/ausstellungen/archiv)

The sum of what is currently publicly available about the artworks in the exhibition.

Sourced from OCR-processed exhibition catalogue held by HsH Library.

Exhibition information (DNB publication record) is included for reference. [https://d-nb.info/957409494](https://d-nb.info/957409494) ISBN [978-3-88375-396-6](https://www.tib.eu/de/suchen/id/gwlb:302796398?cHash=d9b2700b8cf3934df61d65f43f2e6278).

# Introduction

See the [Curator's Guide](00-the-guide.qmd) for more information on how to document exhibitions.     

## Workflows

Workflows can be from active curating project or retrospective documentation of past exhibitions.

### Active projects workflow

Enter data manually into Wikidata, see: Curators' Guide 

### Retrospective workflow

#### OCR Workflow

```text
Book > OCR > Dataset > Wikidata > Publication > Deposit (Mint PIDs)   
```

This is the minimal Linked Open Exhibition process: a source book is converted through OCR into a FAIR dataset, then structured data is published to Wikidata and rendered as a Quarto publication.

## The prototype

The OCR is a R&D LLM processed experiment by Chloë Farr in cooperation with Computational Publishing Service NFDI4Culture @ TIB Open Science Lab with HsH. 

This prototype made by Simon Worthington as part of [Linked Open Exhibition](https://nfdi4culture.github.io/linked-open-exhibition/), an experimental prototype pipeline for publishing art exhibition data as Linked Open Data (LOD). It was created with students of the Bachelor of Arts Information Management at Hochschule Hannover in the course [BIM-126-02 Data Science](https://www.hs-hannover.de/studium/studienangebot/bachelor/information-management/) (SoSe 2026). See Wikiversity link for teaching materials. [https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/BIM-126-02-Data-Science-Linked-Open-Exhibition](https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/BIM-126-02-Data-Science-Linked-Open-Exhibition) (EN/DE).

# Copyright and Licensing

All materials here are open-licenced unless otherwise stated and follow FAIR Data principles and follow UNESCO Open Science recommendations [@unesco2021openscience].

**Source catalogue.** The exhibition data is extracted from the printed catalogue *Baldessari: while something is happening here, something else is happening there: works 1988–1999* (Köln: Verlag der Buchhandlung Walther König, 1999), ISBN [978-3-88375-396-6](https://www.tib.eu/de/suchen/id/gwlb:302796398?cHash=d9b2700b8cf3934df61d65f43f2e6278), DNB record [https://d-nb.info/957409494](https://d-nb.info/957409494). Texts by Meg Cranston, Diedrich Diederichsen and Thomas Weski; published for the exhibition at the Sprengel Museum Hannover (26 September 1999 – 2 January 2000) and the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Gemäldegalerie Neue Meister (16 January – 2 April 2000). The catalogue, including its texts, photographs and reproductions of the artworks, remains protected by copyright held by the publisher, authors, artist and other rights holders. It is not republished here: only factual catalogue data (such as titles, dates, materials, dimensions and catalogue numbers) is extracted and released in the dataset, and no catalogue texts or images are reproduced. The bibliographic record is provided by the Deutsche Nationalbibliothek under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

The project combines several licensing arrangements.

- The software, notebooks, and Quarto source are covered by the repository's existing [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE) terms.
- The catalogue and dataset files in the project are released under [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) and the repository copy is retained in [LICENSE-data](LICENSE-data), so the underlying OCR-derived data may be reused without restriction for research, teaching, and public scholarship.
- For research use, this project also recognises that text and data mining (TDM) may be permitted under the UK and German legal frameworks for scientific research, including UK copyright exceptions and the German research exception in § 60d UrhG. These provisions are jurisdiction-specific and do not replace a review of any third-party rights or source-specific conditions.

This project is configured for:

- Quarto manuscript authoring with `.qmd` files.
- Jupyter notebooks included as project computations.
- Publishing to GitHub Pages.
- Reproducible notebook execution on MyBinder.

# AI LLM use

This project may have utilized AI language models (LLMs) for tasks such as text generation, summarization, or data extraction. Any use of AI LLMs is supplementary and does not replace human authorship or verification of the content.

GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, using Anthropic Claude models (Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5), assisted with the data model documentation, Quarto and Python configuration, notebook set-up and drafting of text. The OCR notebook ([03-catalogue-ocr](notebooks/03-catalogue-ocr.ipynb)) is based on AI LLM use for text extraction. All outputs were reviewed by the authors. See the [TIB AI policy](https://www.tib.eu/en/tib/policies/ai-policy).

The project is aiming to move to open-source and open weight LLM models.
